name: novel_problems/HierarchicalScheduler
prompt:
Write a Java implementation of the concurrency problem described below.
Follow the problem specification and satisfy all implementation requirements.

Problem:
Implement the thread-safe HierarchicalScheduler concurrency problem in Java.
Use HierarchicalScheduler as the public top-level class name.

Contract:
- A scheduler instance represents a node in a dynamically growing reservation
  tree. Provide a root constructor, child(String name), reserve(long start,
  long end), cancel(long reservationId), and snapshot(). Define detached
  reservation and snapshot types in the same file.
- child returns the unique child of this node with that nonempty name,
  creating it if needed. Concurrent calls for the same name must return the
  same fully initialized node. Nodes are never removed or reparented.
- Reservations use half-open intervals [start, end), with start < end.
  A reservation conflicts with overlapping reservations on this node, any
  ancestor, or any descendant. Reservations on separate sibling subtrees
  do not conflict. Touching endpoints do not overlap.
- reserve atomically checks the entire relevant tree and either commits one
  reservation with a tree-wide unique positive ID or returns -1 on conflict.
  It does not wait for availability. cancel removes only a reservation owned
  by this node and returns whether it existed.
- snapshot returns this subtree's node paths and reservations from one
  coherent observation. Returned arrays and records must not expose live
  tree state. A single tree-wide coordinator monitor is permitted.
- Invalid names or intervals throw IllegalArgumentException without mutation.
  Concurrent parent/child reservations for overlapping intervals must never
  both succeed; do not hold node locks in inconsistent ancestor/child order.

Requirements:
- Return a complete, self-contained Java source file.
- Implement the requested behavior yourself; do not use an existing implementation.
- Do not import any libraries or packages. Use only the Java language, primitive
  types, arrays, and classes that are defined in the source file.
- Do not use classes from java.util.concurrent, java.util, or any other
  concurrency or collection library.
- Use only built-in Java synchronization mechanisms and concurrency primitives,
  such as synchronized blocks, intrinsic object monitors, volatile
  fields, wait, notify, and notifyAll. Do not use ReentrantLock, Atomic* classes,
  concurrent collections, or other library-provided synchronization classes.
- Do not use the synchronized modifier in method declarations. Instead, use
  synchronized blocks within the method body.
- Ensure that all public operations are thread-safe and preserve the specified
  invariants when called concurrently by multiple threads.
- Define a clear policy for operations that cannot complete immediately, such as
  a full bounded structure or an empty structure. If operations block, use
  wait/notifyAll correctly and guard waits with while loops.
- Do not use busy-waiting, Thread.sleep, or arbitrary delays as a synchronization mechanism.
- Prevent lost updates, inconsistent state, unsafe publication, and visibility errors.

Output only the Java source code. Do not include Markdown fences, explanations,
tests, or additional files.
